verify_depth.notes: What the cheaper verification depth costs in detection, measured. One model, one small test set, one draw: the 13 fixtures of the pre-registered detection block in tests/fixtures/, 7 planted defects among them, each fixture's hand-written merged.md verified at both depths, K=1 (every figure was identical across K=3 on 2026-09-22, which is the registration's reason for one draw). Figures are per probe direction and never blended: source_to_merged asks whether a source's content survived into the merge, merged_to_sources whether the merge says something its sources do not. cannot_detect names a defect class a depth has no step to reach: coverage has no reverse pass, so a merge that invents a statement (the hallucination fixture) is outside it by construction, and that plant is left out of its rate rather than lowering it. For the same reason coverage grades none of the 28 merged_to_sources guard probes, so its guards_wrong_rate there is null, not zero. plants_detected_mechanically counts plants found by the attributions check, which asks no model and runs at both depths; at coverage it is the only thing that reads the merged document. Scored under the rule, adopted 2026-09-24, that a second report of a detected plant is not an invention; the as-run scoring, which counted full's two second reports on attribution_swapped as invented findings, is kept beside it in the evidence. model_calls and seconds are sums over the 13 fixtures, and speedup is the comparator's seconds over this depth's. Nothing here measures either depth on real documents.
